title: 🚌💷 GLASGOW AREA: £2 BUS FARES HAVE STARTED
message:
Bus passengers across parts of the Strathclyde area can now pay no more than £2 for a single journey on participating services.


This includes areas such as Glasgow, Renfrewshire, Inverclyde, Ayrshire, Lanarkshire and Dunbartonshire.


📍 Check whether your route is included before you travel.

title: 🚨 Your Phone Can Now Prove Your Age
message:
From 15 September 2026, licensed businesses in England and Wales can choose to accept approved digital proof of age when selling alcohol.

This means that at participating pubs, bars, restaurants, shops and other licensed venues, you may be able to prove that you are old enough using an approved app on your phone instead of showing your physical passport or driving licence. 📱

One of the biggest benefits is privacy. Instead of handing over an ID showing details such as your full name, date of birth and address, digital proof of age can simply confirm that you meet the required age threshold.

So, for example, the venue may only need confirmation that you are 18 or over.

But before you leave your physical ID at home 😂👇🏾

⚠️ Not every business has to accept digital proof of age.

The new system is optional for licensed businesses, so some pubs, clubs, restaurants or shops may still ask you to show a physical passport, driving licence or another accepted form of ID.

Your passport and driving licence are not being replaced. Digital proof of age is simply an additional option for businesses that choose to accept it.

📍 Important: This particular change applies to England and Wales.

So for now, if you are heading somewhere where you may be asked for ID, it may still be wise to check the venue’s policy or carry your physical ID until digital proof of age becomes more widely accepted.

💚 Auntie Tobi Tip: Don’t assume every venue will accept your phone just yet. Check first before leaving your physical ID behind.

Know someone who is always forgetting their ID on a night out? 😂 Send this update to them.
pushMessage: From 15 Sept, participating venues in England & Wales can accept approved digital proof of age 📱 But not everywhere accepts it yet—tap to see what changed.

title: 🎒 Year 6 Parents: Apply for Secondary School
message:
🎒 YEAR 6 PARENTS, THIS ONE IS FOR YOU! 👀🇬🇧

Your child has just started Year 6, but secondary school applications for September 2027 are already opening across England. And yes, the deadline will come around faster than you think. 😊

If you haven’t started looking at schools yet, here are four things to do now:

1️⃣ Shortlist the secondary schools you’re interested in.

2️⃣ Check their open evening dates and, where possible, visit with your child.

3️⃣ Read the admissions criteria. Catchment areas, sibling priority, faith-school requirements and other rules can affect how places are allocated.

4️⃣ Check your local council’s application opening date and submit before the deadline.

📅 The national deadline for secondary school applications in England is 31 October 2026. Applications open on different dates depending on your council, so check yours now.

And please, don’t assume your child will automatically get a place because their primary school is linked to a secondary school or because an older sibling attends. You still need to apply.
pushMessage: Secondary school applications for September 2027 are opening across England.

title: 🚨 UK Workers: Employment Rights Are Changing From October 2026
message:
More employment-law changes are coming in the UK from October 2026.


One of the biggest changes is that employers will be expected to take all reasonable steps to prevent sexual harassment at work, with stronger responsibilities around harassment involving third parties such as customers, clients or service users.


There are more changes coming after that too.


From 1 January 2027, the qualifying period for ordinary unfair-dismissal protection is due to reduce from 2 years to 6 months.


Who should pay attention?

This matters to:

  • Employees

  • Agency and temporary workers

  • Managers and supervisors

  • Business owners

  • Employers

  • HR teams


Why it matters

Some people still assume they need to work for an employer for years before gaining meaningful workplace protection.

The rules are changing.


Employers should be reviewing their policies, training and complaint procedures now, while workers should understand their rights before problems happen.


⚠️ Important: The October changes are not in force yet. They are due to start from October 2026, with further reforms from January 2027.


💚 Auntie Tobi Says:
Don’t wait until something goes wrong at work before learning your rights.


Source: HMRC Employer Bulletin / UK employment-law reforms.
pushMessage: New UK worker protections start October 2026 with more changes coming in January 2027. Tap to see what’s changing.
